title: A coherent module supported in the zero set of an ideal is killed by a power of it
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] with quasi-compact underlying space), $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] and $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, with $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F$ as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0) for $t\ge1$ and $\mathcal K^0\mathcal F=\mathcal F$; let $V(\mathcal K)=\{x\in X:\mathcal K_x\ne\mathcal O_{X,x}\}$ (the closed subset underlying the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal K$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is $V(\mathcal K(\operatorname{Spec}A))$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine]). Then $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F=0$ for some $t\ge0$ if and only if $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\subseteq V(\mathcal K)$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf, line 2569); its proof: a finite covering by spectra of Noetherian rings and Algebra, Lemma 00L6 (algebra-lemma-Noetherian-power-ideal-kills-module, algebra.tex line 14997)

proof.text: *Step 1 (a finite affine cover with Noetherian rings).* By [pqf-def-locnoeth] $X$ has an affine open covering by opens $U$ with $\mathcal O_X(U)$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; since $X$ is quasi-compact, finitely many of them, $U_1,\dots,U_r$, cover $X$. Put $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$, a Noetherian ring, and identify $U_i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (an affine scheme, the identification inducing the identity on global sections), $x\in U_i$ corresponding to the prime $\mathfrak p_x\subset A_i$. ('$X$ has a finite covering by spectra of Noetherian rings.')

*Step 2 ($M_i=\mathcal F(U_i)$ is a finite $A_i$-module).* $\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], so of finite type, and of finite presentation: every point has an open $W$ with a surjection $\pi:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$, whose kernel is of finite type by coherence, so on a smaller open $V\ni x$ there is a surjection $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\operatorname{Ker}(\pi)|_V$ and $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_V\to0$ is exact. Hence $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](0), and, being quasi-coherent of finite type, $M_i=\mathcal F(U_i)$ is a finitely generated $A_i$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] for every $i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), proof (the finite module on each member of the covering; Properties, Lemma 01PB, carried by lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the sections of $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F$ on $U_i$).* Put $I_i=\mathcal K(U_i)$, an ideal of $A_i$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal O_X$: every $\mathcal K^s$ ($s\ge1$) is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with $\mathcal K^s(U_i)=I_i^s$ (part (1) and (2)). Applying it to the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J=\mathcal K^t$ ($t\ge1$) and the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ (Step 2): $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F$ (the image of $\mathcal K^t\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, notation of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0)) is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module (part (1)) and $(\mathcal K^t\mathcal F)(U_i)=\mathcal K^t(U_i)\,\mathcal F(U_i)=I_i^tM_i$ (part (2)). For $t=0$, $\mathcal K^0\mathcal F=\mathcal F$ and $I_i^0M_i=M_i$, so $(\mathcal K^t\mathcal F)(U_i)=I_i^tM_i$ for every $t\ge0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), proof (the reduction to modules over the rings of the covering, written out by the agent)

proof.text: *Step 4 ($\mathcal K^t\mathcal F=0$ iff $I_i^tM_i=0$ for all $i$).* If $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F=0$ then its sections $I_i^tM_i$ (Step 3) are $0$. Conversely let $I_i^tM_i=0$ for $i=1,\dots,r$ and put $\mathcal G=\mathcal K^t\mathcal F$, quasi-coherent (Step 3). Fix $i$. The restriction $\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2), with global sections $\mathcal G(U_i)=0$; transported to $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\cong U_i$ (Step 1), the counit $\widetilde{\mathcal G(U_i)}=\widetilde 0\to\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3), and $\widetilde 0=0$ ($0$ is the colimit of the empty diagram of $A_i$-modules, so $\widetilde 0$ is the colimit of the empty diagram, the zero module, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4)). So $\mathcal G(V)=0$ for every open $V\subseteq U_i$. For any open $V\subseteq X$ and $s\in\mathcal G(V)$, $s|_{V\cap U_i}=0$ for all $i$, and the $V\cap U_i$ cover $V$, so $s=0$ by the sheaf property [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Hence $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F=0$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), proof (the passage from the covering to $X$, written out by the agent as in the proof of Lemma 01Y8)

proof.text: *Step 5 (support and zero set on $U_i$).* As $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type (Step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] gives, for $x\in U_i$: $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ iff $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_i}(M_i)\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$, i.e. $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\cap U_i=V(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_i}(M_i))$ (which is $\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], Algebra, Lemma 00L2). By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine], $V(\mathcal K)\cap U_i=V(I_i)$. Since $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_r$, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\subseteq V(\mathcal K)$ holds iff $V(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_i}(M_i))\subseteq V(I_i)$ for every $i$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y9 (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), proof; Algebra, Lemma 00L2 (lemma-support-closed) as used in the proof of Lemma 00L6

proof.text: *Step 6 (Algebra, Lemma 00L6 on each $U_i$).* Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $M$ a finite $A$-module, $\mathfrak a=\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)$. Then: (a) for $n\ge0$, $I^nM=0$ iff $I^n\subseteq\mathfrak a$ (definition of the annihilator, as $I^nM$ is generated by the $am$, $a\in I^n$); (b) if $I^n\subseteq\mathfrak a$ then $V(\mathfrak a)\subseteq V(I)$: a prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq\mathfrak a$ contains $I^n$, hence $I$ ($a\in I$ gives $a^n\in\mathfrak p$, so $a\in\mathfrak p$; for $n=0$, $\mathfrak a=A$ and $V(\mathfrak a)=\emptyset$); (c) if $V(\mathfrak a)\subseteq V(I)$, then $I\subseteq\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in V(\mathfrak a)}\mathfrak p=\sqrt{\mathfrak a}$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] (Algebra, Lemma 00E0); $I$ is finitely generated since $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $I^n\subseteq\mathfrak a$ for some $n\ge1$ [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] (Algebra, Lemma 00IM), i.e. $I^nM=0$ by (a); and then $I^mM\subseteq I^nM=0$ for every $m\ge n$. Applied to $(A_i,I_i,M_i)$ (Steps 1, 2, 3): $I_i^tM_i=0$ for some $t$ iff $V(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_i}(M_i))\subseteq V(I_i)$, and then $I_i^{t'}M_i=0$ for all $t'\ge t$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00L6 (lemma-Noetherian-power-ideal-kills-module, line 14997), proof: via Lemma 00IM (lemma-Noetherian-power), Lemma 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology) and Lemma 00L2 (lemma-support-closed)

proof.text: *Step 7 (conclusion; uniform $t$).* If $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F=0$, then $I_i^tM_i=0$ for all $i$ (Step 4), so $V(\operatorname{Ann}_{A_i}(M_i))\subseteq V(I_i)$ for all $i$ (Step 6), i.e. $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\subseteq V(\mathcal K)$ (Step 5). Conversely, if $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\subseteq V(\mathcal K)$, Step 5 and Step 6 give for each $i$ an $n_i$ with $I_i^{m}M_i=0$ for all $m\ge n_i$; put $t=\max(n_1,\dots,n_r)$ (finitely many $i$; $t=0$ if $r=0$, i.e. $X=\emptyset$). Then $I_i^tM_i=0$ for all $i$, so $\mathcal K^t\mathcal F=0$ by Step 4.
